name: The Remote Work Haven
tagline: Fast wifi, good coffee, zero commute.
description: Towns that figured out early that a laptop and a decent signal can replace a skyscraper. Expect coworking spaces in old storefronts, a coffee shop that knows your order, and enough outdoor access that logging off actually feels like something.

name: The Retirement Retreat
tagline: Nowhere to be, and all day to get there.
description: Slower mornings, easier parking, neighbors who wave. These towns trade ambition for ease — walkable enough for a cane or a golf cart, quiet enough that the loudest thing on the block is a lawnmower.

name: The Foodie's Table
tagline: One traffic light, three restaurants worth a drive.
description: Disproportionately good food for their size, usually because a chef got tired of the city and a farmer had land to spare. The kind of place where the tasting menu changes with what came in that morning.

name: The Coastal Charmer
tagline: Salt air, sandy floors, tide charts on the fridge.
description: Built around a shoreline and proud of it. Life runs on tide charts and sunset timing, the architecture leans toward shingles and shutters, and everyone owns exactly one nice sweater for the off-season.

name: The Mountain Hideaway
tagline: Trailhead at the edge of town, cell signal optional.
description: Elevation changes everything — the light, the pace, the size of your jacket collection. These towns exist because the mountains were worth building next to, and they still act like it.

name: The Creative Enclave
description: Somewhere along the way, artists found cheap rent and good light, and never left. Now the old feed store is a gallery, the diner hosts open mic on Thursdays, and the town's whole personality runs on what people make with their hands.

name: The Family Hometown
tagline: Good schools, cul-de-sacs, everyone knows your kid's name.
description: Built for the long haul — strong schools, safe streets, a Fourth of July parade that actually shuts down Main Street. The kind of place people move to on purpose and then never quite leave.

name: College Town Energy
tagline: Twenty thousand students and a stadium you can hear from downtown.
description: A permanent undercurrent of youth keeps these towns loud, cheap to eat in, and never quite finished changing. Great bookstores, better bars, and a fall Saturday that reorders the whole town's schedule.
